extracted.intended_audience: educators and graduate students involved in teaching or learning grant-writing and service-learning (program evaluators, writing instructors)
extracted.subtask_short: teaching grant writing with service learning
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and assessing a service-learning grant-writing assignment in a multidisciplinary masters-level program evaluation course where students ghost-write proposals for community organizations; projects are evaluated and outcomes (student and sponsor) are measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty judge ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects were assessed by ratings provided by faculty across departments who served as judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses cross-departmental faculty as judges to rate student grant proposals. The article gives no numeric scoring rubric or explicit criteria used by judges; this indicates expert faculty evaluation as a primary assessment method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational sponsor satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative data was collected from students and organizational sponsors that showed high levels of satisfaction from both groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor feedback/satisfaction is treated as an outcome measure; collection appears qualitative (e.g., interviews or surveys). Use sponsor satisfaction to judge the usefulness and acceptability of student-produced proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student learning outcomes and writing experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant writing experience can be a valuable asset for students completing masters-level degree programs across a variety of disciplines. Twelve students served as 'ghost writers' and wrote grant proposals to foundations for community organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess students on gains in grant-writing skills, fulfillment of course writing requirements, perceived value for career/degree, and satisfaction. The study treats student perception and skill development as key evaluative dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity of benefit from service learning
rubrics_metrics.description: An awareness of reciprocity of benefit from service learning were observed in both groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the service-learning arrangement produced mutual benefit for students and community organizations (reciprocity). The article highlights perceived mutual benefits as an important qualitative outcome to document.
